title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Quarter-Wave Seeded Initialization (20 Layers)
scientific_hypothesis: Physics-informed quarter-wave thickness initialization centered at λ=4.45μm (midpoint between CO and CO2 bands) will reduce search-space entropy and accelerate convergence toward resonant stacking conditions compared to uniform 500nm initialization, while maintaining the verified Ge/ZnS two-cavity topology.
design_principle: Start from alternating quarter-wave layers (H=L=λ/4n) at band center, then apply computational optimization to adjust thicknesses for dual-bandpass profile with stopband blocking. Two Fabry-Perot cavities coupled in series shape the passband.
proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Ge/ZnS]_10 stack (20 finite layers) | Air superstrate. Explicit sequence: Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS
design_variables: 20 layer thicknesses with quarter-wave seeded bounds
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm bands
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack resonance condition: d_k = λ_center/(4*n_k)
Fabry-Perot cavity transmittance maximum when (φ1+φ2-2δ)/2 = kπ
Higher index contrast (Ge/ZnS) reduces required film thickness and increases maximum transmittance
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to physics-informed initialization
Maintains verified Ge/ZnS material performance from prior iteration
Quarter-wave seeding reduces risk of local minima far from resonant condition
known_risks: Quarter-wave at single center wavelength may not optimally serve dual-band requirement
20 layers may limit stopband depth compared to higher layer counts
Fabrication tolerances may cause measured transmittance to decrease relative to theoretical
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer Ge/ZnS multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-bandpass transmission. Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave formula d_k = 4450nm/(4*n_k) where n_Ge≈4.0 and n_ZnS≈2.2 at 4.45μm center wavelength, giving initial Ge thickness ≈278nm and ZnS thickness ≈506nm. Set optimization bounds to ±40% around quarter-wave values (Ge: 167-389nm, ZnS: 304-708nm). Wavelength bands: transmit 4150-4350nm and 4550-4750nm, block 3600-4000nm and 4850-5200nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized. Max 24 layers constraint satisfied with 20 layers. No metal layers. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with coherent TMM across all bands. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Implementing feedback directive to replace uniform 500nm initialization with physics-informed quarter-wave targets. Maintains verified Ge/ZnS 20-layer topology from route_01 which achieved 0.978 target score.
